html:
The Puinave are an Indigenous people of the Inírida and Guaviare rivers, in eastern Colombia and the neighbouring part of Venezuela, in the basin of the Orinoco. They call themselves Wãnsöhöt. Their language is usually counted as an isolate.

They lived by fishing, hunting and growing manioc in forest gardens. In the 1700s Spanish missions and slave raids reached the upper Orinoco, and in the late 1800s the rubber boom drew many into forced labour. From the 1940s an evangelical mission converted most Puinave to Protestant Christianity. Today several thousand Puinave live in reserves in Colombia's Guainía department.
